newsitem.title: INDIA: No India labour law easing in 2-3 yrs - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: No India labour law easing in 2-3 yrs - Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Tuesday that he did not expect laws shielding workers' rights to be relaxed in the next two or three years.
Chidambaram said there was no political consensus in favour of industry's oft-repeated demand for the relaxation of labour law governing the hiring and firing of workers.
"There is no proposal at the moment to change the law, to provide for a more flexible labour policy," he told the World Economic Forum. "I can't see that happening in the next two or three years."
Many companies argue that the laws prevent them from reducing their work-force during an economic slowdown and from hiring new employees during a period of economic expansion.
But left-wing political parties in Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's ruling coalition strongly oppose any loosening of the labour laws to favour business.
